summary: The study investigates the use of ultrathin Al2O3 interlayers deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) to reduce gate leakage current in TiO2/Ge interfaces for scaled Ge-channel metal-oxide-semiconductor devices. The ALD-Al2O3 interlayer significantly reduces gate leakage by six orders of magnitude at flatband voltage, demonstrating its effectiveness in passivating the interface and enabling subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.
evidence: ALD-Al2O3 ILs of 0.8, 1.2, and 3 nm thicknesses were deposited at 250 °C from a trimethyl aluminum (TMA)/H2O process. The introduction of an ultrathin Al2O3 IL reduces the leakage current significantly, by approximately six orders of magnitude at the flatband voltage. The hysteresis of the capacitance-voltage curves was ±10 mV for TiO2/Al2O3/Ge capacitors with different Al2O3 thicknesses.
